name: Commenter AI
tagline: An AI product that drafts LinkedIn comments and DMs in the user's own voice, and keeps the conversations that matter in one place.
description: Commenter AI helps founders, salespeople, and recruiters stay active in conversations without writing every reply from scratch. I worked across the product: the workflows people use, the data behind them, the channel integrations, and the AI drafting. The public product learns a person's tone, suggests comments they can edit, and tracks who they have engaged with so warm leads are not buried in a feed.

problem: People who sell or recruit live in LinkedIn comments, DMs, email, and meetings. The useful threads get buried, writing a good reply takes too long, and generic AI drafts sound nothing like the person sending them.
approach: Organize the conversations that need a response, then draft in the user's voice instead of generating a post they would never send. The user picks the tone, edits the line, and posts it themselves.
solution: A product for daily commenting and follow-up. It learns tone from a short setup and from comments the user actually posts, drafts replies they can shorten or rewrite, and keeps a record of who they have engaged with and what should happen next. A custom newsfeed limits the feed to the people and topics they care about. The same commenting workflow is aimed at LinkedIn, with X, Meta, and Instagram in the product as well.
features: Drafts comments in the user's voice, with controls for tone, length, emotion, and formality
User reviews and posts the reply. Nothing is sent automatically
Custom newsfeed so engagement stays on the right people and topics
Lightweight CRM of who they have talked to, how often, and what comes next
Built around comments and replies, not generic post generation
Onboarding that learns a voice from a few questions, then improves from comments they post
Web product plus iOS and Android apps
architecture: Full-stack product with channel integrations and an AI drafting layer. Conversation and engagement data is stored so the app can rank what needs attention and keep next steps attached to the person, not only to the latest message.
